title: In reply [to the comment on: “Timing of arthrocentesis and its association with treatment success in painful temporomandibular joint disorders: a two-decade cohort study”]
html: We thank the correspondents for their interest in our study1, and for providing their thoughtful comments. Our study evaluated the association between the timing of initial temporomandibular joint (TMJ) arthrocentesis and patient-reported treatment success. The findings of this study specifically concern arthrocentesis rather than minimally invasive surgery as a whole. Furthermore, TMJ arthroscopy was neither investigated nor discussed, and no data was collected that was related to arthroscopy. Therefore, we agree that the results of the current study should be interpreted exclusively in the context of TMJ arthrocentesis, and should not be extrapolated to TMJ arthroscopy.
